I farm only 2.0 mu, so I will keep the whole plot in maize and manage it carefully rather than diversify. In Quzhou County, with my experience and with access to well irrigation, I will use hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence, stronger vigor, and higher yield potential on a small area where every mu matters. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and gives me a clean seedbed. I will apply a moderate-to-strong fertilizer program: enough nitrogen to support maize growth, with phosphorus and potassium to support rooting, grain filling, and stand strength. Since I have irrigation, I will not rely only on rainfall; I will plan a few irrigations at the key growth stages to reduce risk. I will also spray pesticides only as needed but expect at least two applications across the season to control early and mid-season pests and protect yield. With this approach, I will aim for a solid maize harvest from the full 2.0 mu.
